reason: Reverts PR #284, which wired the <culture> context block into the tag path and the participation turn. Nothing a member of a room could observe changes: the block was inert behind [culture] enabled = false, the shipped default, so it never rendered in any deployment. It comes out because it violated its own design bundle's preconditions, all four of which design/culture-tier/02-measurement.md had recorded before it shipped. §5 step 5 requires the chronicle-vs-account eval arm to ship WITH the block, in one change — a constraint PR #279 added the day before precisely to govern this step — and the block shipped with zero eval coverage. §6 states the decision check is not optional for this block and that if it cannot move a labelled metric the honest conclusion is that it does not ship into that prompt; no decision check was run. §5 step 3, let it run and get a baseline, was skipped: the block landed eight hours after the store it reads, which is empty by construction while the tier is off. And 01-the-adaptor §6 names exactly one consumer, the participation turn, while PR #284 also wired the tag path, the highest-traffic prompt in the system, which no design decision authorises. This is a revert of premature wiring and not a rejection of the code: its primary_id-rather-than-conversation_id key resolution was careful and correct, and is to be reinstated verbatim when the block re-ships beside its measurement arm. The renderer nora/language/culture_render.py, the store, the migration, the Dreamer adaptor and its schedule all stay — only the read wiring is removed.
